findings.title: Call to non-existent no-arg isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() breaks compilation
findings.body:
`UsernameForm.authenticate` calls `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` with no arguments. The only method this PR adds to the superclass `UsernamePasswordForm` is `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)`, and there is no no-arg overload. The services module therefore does not compile.

The call should pass the current user: `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())`. Even after that fix, the skip decision for re-authentication depends on the predicate in `UsernamePasswordForm`, which is itself wrong (see the separate finding).

findings.title: isConditionalPasskeysEnabled requires user != null, disabling passkeys on normal login
findings.body:
The new helper returns `webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled() && user != null`. Both `authenticate()` and the error `challenge()` now gate `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context)` on it. On a fresh login `context.getUser()` is null, so the conditional-UI passkey data (challenge, `ENABLE_WEBAUTHN_CONDITIONAL_UI`, the webauth form) is never added. That is the primary passkey use case, and the old code explicitly filled it when the user was null.

The same applies after a failed initial login. `validateUserAndPassword` clears the context user, so the error re-challenge also drops passkeys.

The new tests that expect automatic discoverable-key login or the `//form[@id='webauth']` element on the initial page would fail, e.g. `webauthnLoginWithDiscoverableKey` and the first half of the `_reauthentication` tests.

Conversely, when a user is set (re-authentication), the passkey UI is enabled for any user, even one with no passkey credential. `UsernameForm` would then never skip the username step during re-auth for such users.

The intended condition is likely `user == null || user.credentialManager().isConfiguredFor(webauthnAuth.getCredentialType())`.

findings.title: reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey disables passkeys realm-wide instead of testing a user without a passkey
findings.body:
The test name and the comment at line 304 ("Passkeys login should not be available on the page as this user does not have passkey") claim to verify that a user with no passkey credential does not see passkey UI during re-authentication. The test, however, sets `setWebAuthnPolicyPasskeysEnabled(Boolean.FALSE)` for the whole realm, so the webauth form is absent only because the feature is off.

The case this PR actually changes is never covered: passkeys enabled for the realm, re-authenticating user has only a password. In that case the current `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled` would show the passkey UI.

The comment at line 280 ("set passwordless policy for discoverable keys") is also wrong for this block. A test with passkeys enabled and a password-only user (e.g. test-user@localhost) should be added.
